page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.32-256 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC architecture. It is provisioned with 32 dedicated physical AMD EPYC 7742 processor cores running at a base clock frequency of 2.25 GHz, providing 64 vCPUs through simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is allocated at 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU.

The instance features dedicated CPU allocation without fractional scheduling or burstable credits. It contains no onboard local NVMe storage, meaning persistent storage requirements must be handled using remote network-attached block storage volumes. The profile includes no GPU acceleration hardware. For external connectivity, one complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the instance.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance and dedicated x86_64 compute cores, the VM.Standard.E3.Flex.32-256 is structured for horizontally scaled enterprise services. Key workload fits include container orchestration nodes, multi-tier web application servers, continuous integration workflows, batch processing tasks, and relational databases backed by external block storage.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.32-256 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7742 processor. Configured with 32 physical cores and simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz alongside 256.0 GB of system memory. This yields a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote network-attached block volumes for persistent data. No GPU accelerators are present in this shape. Network connectivity is supported with one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated compute resources and a standard memory footprint per core, this instance is suited for multi-tier enterprise workloads, backend application servers, container clusters, batch processing, and continuous integration pipelines requiring predictable multi-threaded CPU performance.
